title: Hampi
summary: Hampi in Karnataka is the ruined capital of the Vijayanagara kingdom, a Hindu state whose rulers built large Dravidian temples and palaces in the 14th to 16th centuries. After Deccan sultanates conquered the city in 1565 it was plundered and abandoned.

uncertainty.note: The ASI dates the monuments to 1336-1570; UNESCO describes the city between the 14th and 16th centuries and its conquest in 1565. End is the present: the ruins survive.

as_recorded.value: Conquered by the Deccan Muslim confederacy in 1565

when.display: Monuments built 1336–1570 CE; sacked 1565; ruins stand today

where.modern_name: Group of Monuments at Hampi, Vijayanagara district, Karnataka, India
where.historical_name: Vijayanagara, capital of the Vijayanagara kingdom

importance.justification: UNESCO calls it the last capital of the last great Hindu kingdom; the ASI notes remains over about 26 sq km within seven lines of fortification.
